thread:
deploy-bot: Deploy finished: inference-gateway v2.13 -> prod (commit: f8a9d2)
Lena: seeing a small burst in 5xx right after the deploy, p95 looks fine but p99 jumping. anyone else? :eyes:
Marco: yep, dashboards show p99 from 350ms -> 3.2s on /v1/generate starting at +2m post-deploy. error rate 3% 5xx/timeouts.
Noah: paging oncall- pinging current oncall @SRE-Lead
oncall-bot: @SRE-Lead, you were paged for incident: svc=inference-gateway severity=high
SRE-Lead: on it. linking logs and traces. does the Canary show the same?
Lena: Canary was clean. This roll was a full-traffic cutover from canary at t0 + 30s. timeline: canary -> promote -> full -> spike at +2m.
Marco: correlating with deploy logs, the new runtime changed connection pool defaults (max_inflight=64 -> 32). suspect pool exhaustion under bursty multiplexing.
Noah: customer impact? Support-Escalations, any active tickets?
Support-Escalations: a few 500s reported by internal QA and one external error alert from a low-volume customer. No major rollback requests yet.
Lena: let's reduce surface area: target older model variant and ramp traffic back to previous gateway version. Can we route 100% to fallback-model-v1 via routing rule?
Marco: I can add a routing override. Applying: `redwood route update inference-gateway --model fallback-model-v1 --weight 100`
Marco: applied. Confirming traffic shift.
oncall-bot: Routing change initiated by Marco.
Lena: nice, p99 back to ~420ms within 40s of routing change. error rate trending down.
SRE-Lead: still seeing occasional timeouts at the gateway layer. Let's revert the gateway binary if we see any plateau. Are there any long tail traces showing KV cache misses?
Marco: quick grep of traces shows many requests stuck waiting on backend muxer: `muxer_wait > 1.5s` and TCP wait counts rose.
Noah: rolling back deploy now? We should decide: rollback binary or patch pool config. Rolling back is faster for safety.
Lena: agree. Marco, trigger rollback. Marco, ping deploy-bot with rollback command.
Marco: `deploy-bot: rollback inference-gateway to previous release (commit: e2b7c1)`
deploy-bot: Rollback started by Marco — downtime window minimal, performing blue/green switch.
Noah: heads up to customers: posting status update draft: "We detected elevated timeouts after a recent deploy affecting a small subset of requests. We are reverting the deploy and monitoring. More updates in 15m." Approve? :+1:
Support-Escalations: approved. Post it.
Lena: rollback completed. deploy-bot: rollback finished -> prod stable (commit: e2b7c1).
deploy-bot: Active instances: 48 -> 48, health checks green.
Marco: p99 back to pre-deploy levels ~380ms. 5xx down to baseline.
SRE-Lead: good. mark incident mitigated, start collecting evidence for postmortem: timeline, diff of connection pool defaults, trace snippets, routing change timestamps, customer impact notes.
Lena: creating an incident ticket and adding owners. I'll assign the postmortem to Marco + Networking + Runtime @two people.
Noah: immediate action items: 1) add canary soak time >= 5m for this service, 2) make pool config explicit in deploy manifest (don't rely on defaults), 3) add an alert on muxer_wait > 500ms for >1m.
Marco: logging the config fix in PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/834 - will add explicit max_inflight and connection backoff.
Support-Escalations: customer notification posted. no escalations received after rollback.
SRE-Lead: handing off to morning oncall for postmortem follow-up. tagging owners in ticket.
Lena: thanks everyone. Adding last note: we observed a narrow window where the runtime default change exposed a capacity cliff under multiplexed clients. next steps in postmortem should focus on safer defaults and stronger canary gating. :memo:
Marco: +1 and will run a targeted load test on the combination of multiplexing + lower max_inflight tomorrow.
Noah: closing slack incident thread, will keep the ticket open until PM complete.
deploy-bot: Incident closed (mitigated).
